source.title: Large Language Models for Limited Noisy Data: A Gravitational Wave Identification Study
source.authors: Yixuan Li; Yu-Hao Lu; Yang Liu; Liang Li; R. Ruffini; Di Li; Rong-Gen Cai; Xiao-Yan Zhu; Wenbin Lin; Yu Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including conclusions and references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream classification accuracy across model and dataset sizes, a different measure and setting from the held-out pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The scaling experiments report classification accuracy, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy, fitted power laws, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocations. The paper's claims about other astronomical domains are suggestions, not experiments. Rows below record the downstream-accuracy scaling results and the reported simulation-pretraining comparison; cited scaling-law results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Fine-tuned LLM families are swept from 0.5B to 8B parameters on a gravitational-wave classification task, and test accuracy is reported against model size. This is a new-setting downstream result bearing on V6, but only qualitatively: no power law is fitted and pretraining loss is not measured. Scaling is not the paper's main aim, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that LoRA-fine-tuned LLMs reach 97.4% accuracy using only 90 LIGO events, and that simulated pre-finetuning adds nothing. The scaling results are secondary: accuracy rises with model size, with families converging near 8B, and with dataset size, with diminishing gains. The authors call these 'predictable' and consistent with scaling-law trends, but fit no law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fine-tuned models on gravitational-wave classification and measures task accuracy across model and dataset sizes, rather than fitting held-out pretraining-loss power laws or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported magnitude of model-size improvement depends on architecture in the small-to-mid scale range; dataset-size gains become less steep near the upper end of the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: Simulation pre-finetuning on 560k G2Net samples gave no measurable gain on observational test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large simulated pre-finetuning data adds no benefit for LLM gravitational-wave identification.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA3-8B accuracy rises with fine-tuning set size (300–60k samples, about 1.2M–240M tokens), with diminishing gains at the top of the range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy grows with fine-tuning data size, with saturating returns; no power-law fit is given.

record.problems: The scaling results are task accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss and do not fit power laws or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocations. The reported size sweeps use simulated data, and the text gives few exact accuracy values; variability is shown across only three runs. The simulation-pretraining comparison reports no measurable gain but gives no exact numerical difference in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the claim were left out. The observational-data accuracy result is not a scaling result; the proposed application to other astronomical domains is not experimentally tested.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit for fine-tuning or the new domain; fine-tuning data scaling is only described qualitatively.
No quantitative fit or prediction of accuracy. No relation to pretraining loss. Nothing beyond 8B. Exact per-size values are not given in the text.
No exponents are fitted or compared.

record.verdict_notes: All scaling sweeps use LoRA fine-tuning on a downstream binary task, with accuracy only around 0.70. No pretraining loss is measured and no fits are made, so the bearing on V6 is weak and qualitative. 'Predictable' in the abstract is not backed by any fitted relation.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute is not measured.
No small-run loss fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is evaluated.
The paper compares model families on task accuracy, not loss across architecture variants at fixed parameter count.
The study uses gravitational-wave data, but does not test whether a power-law form in held-out loss transfers to other modalities or training regimes.
It reports qualitative downstream accuracy trends with model and dataset size, but does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or establish a quantitative predictive law.
No loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: LLaMA3
rows.size_stated: 0.5 billion to 8 billion parameters across the tested family; exact checkpoints not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated classification accuracy across model parameter sizes.
rows.value: Accuracy increases with parameter size; LLaMA3 is above 0.69 at the 1B scale.
rows.uncertainty: Variability across three runs is shown as standard deviation; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text describes the size trend and gives the 1B result; other point values are plotted but not stated numerically.
rows.check: LLaMA3 is already above 0.69 at 1B and reaches only about 0.70–0.72 near 8B. That is a small gain, not a full scaling trend.

rows.size_stated: 0.5 billion to 8 billion parameters across the tested family; exact checkpoints not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated classification accuracy across model parameter sizes.
rows.value: Accuracy improves more gradually, with substantial gains only once parameter count exceeds several billion.
rows.uncertainty: Variability across three runs is shown as standard deviation; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The paper reports a qualitative trend; point values are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5, LLaMA3, and DeepSeek (reported together)
rows.operation_detail: Compared model-family accuracy at the largest tested parameter scale.
rows.value: The families converge to accuracies around 0.70–0.72, with small variance across repeated trials.
rows.uncertainty: Small variance across repeated trials; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: This is the paper's aggregate description of the three families at approximately 7–8B.
rows.check: This is convergence of families at about 8B, a cross-family comparison at one size, not a trend with scale. The families differ in pretraining, so it is not a V4 shape test either.

rows.subject: LLaMA3 8-billion model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy with progressively larger training sets.

conditions.value: three independent runs per dataset configuration

rows.value: Accuracy rises as dataset size increases; gains become less steep near the upper end of the tested range.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation across three runs is shown; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The trend and diminishing gains are described in the text; individual dataset-size accuracies are not given numerically.
rows.check: The sweep varies fine-tuning data size (300–60k samples), not pretraining scale, so it does not bear on V6. No power-law form is fitted, so it cannot test V5. Diminishing gains are expected under scaling, so the reader's 'partial' state is unwarranted; moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: LLM (model not specified in Section 4.1)
rows.stage_stated: simulation pre-finetuning followed by fine-tuning on observational data
rows.operation_detail: Pre-finetuned on simulated data, then fine-tuned on observational data and evaluated on a held-out observational test set.
rows.baseline: Performance after fine-tuning on observational data alone; exact value not stated in Section 4.1.
rows.value: Reported as essentially unchanged; no measurable improvement from simulation-based pre-finetuning.
rows.note: This bears on the broader subject of data-regime effects on downstream performance, but does not test a claim version about loss scaling or predictability.

relationships.condition: DeepSeek and Qwen2.5, 0.5B–8B, fine-tuned on 3,000 simulated G2Net samples
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with parameter count, with substantial gains past several billion parameters (R2, R3). This is qualitative only.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased with parameter count, with substantial gains beyond several billion parameters.

relationships.reason: Accuracy is already above 0.69 at 1B and about 0.70–0.72 at 8B, so model size adds little here (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy already exceeded 0.69 at 1B and reached only about 0.70–0.72 at 8B.
